title: Profinite sets as pro-étale $\Spec\Z$-schemes
statement:
Let $*_{\mathrm{proét}}$ be the category of profinite sets
([sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring]). The functor
$$
u\colon *_{\mathrm{proét}}\longrightarrow(\Spec\Z)_{\mathrm{proét}},\qquad
S\longmapsto\bigl(\Spec LC(S,\Z)\to\Spec\Z\bigr),
$$
takes values in the small pro-étale site of $\Spec\Z$
([def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]). On morphisms, $u$ sends a continuous map
$g\colon S'\to S$ to the morphism $\Spec LC(S',\Z)\to\Spec LC(S,\Z)$ induced
by the ring map $LC(S,\Z)\to LC(S',\Z)$, $h\mapsto h\circ g$.

proof.text:
By [lem-sfb-lc-weakly-etale], $\Spec LC(S,\Z)\to\Spec\Z$ is weakly étale, so
$u(S)$ is an object of $(\Spec\Z)_{\mathrm{proét}}$. The composite of a
locally constant function with a continuous map is again locally constant, so
$h\mapsto h\circ g$ is a well-defined ring map. The induced morphism of
spectra lies over $\Spec\Z$ because $\Spec\Z$ is terminal. Precomposition
respects identities and composites, and so does $\Spec$. Hence $u$ is a
functor.
